question.text: A solid sphere of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is rotated about one of its diameter with angular speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the moment of inertia of the sphere about its tangent is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> times its angular momentum about the diameter. Then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be

solution.text:
The angular momentum about the diameter is 

Ldiameter =25MR2ω;

The moment of inertia of a sphere is ICM=25MR2. The moment of inertia about the tangent is 

Itangent =ICM+MR2=25MR2+MR2=75MR2.

It is given that ω=10 rad s-1

Using the given relation between the moment of inertia and the angular momentum,

75MR2=x×10-2×25MR2ω⇒x=3.5×102ω=3.5×10=35
